title: Alundra
publisher: Sony Computer Entertainment / Working Designs / Psygnosis
subtitle: The village behind the nightmares
summary: Alundra is Matrix Software's PlayStation action-adventure, first released in Japan on 11 April 1997. A young dreamwalker survives a shipwreck and reaches Inoa, a village whose people suffer recurring nightmares. His ability to enter those dreams gives him a way to help, but deaths and suspicion gradually make the refuge less welcoming. The island and its dungeons combine exploration, real-time combat and demanding puzzles. The setting gives those familiar activities a personal connection: the next strange place may exist inside someone met earlier in the village.
body: Alundra is Matrix Software's PlayStation action-adventure, first released in Japan on 11 April 1997. A young dreamwalker survives a shipwreck and reaches Inoa, a village whose people suffer recurring nightmares. His ability to enter those dreams gives him a way to help, but deaths and suspicion gradually make the refuge less welcoming. The island and its dungeons combine exploration, real-time combat and demanding puzzles. The setting gives those familiar activities a personal connection: the next strange place may exist inside someone met earlier in the village.

Each dream reflects the person experiencing it, allowing the adventure to change its surroundings without leaving the villagers behind. Outside those sequences, Alundra searches an island of terrain and obstacles that react differently to his movement. Sand slows him and lava causes damage; later improvements can make previously difficult routes manageable. Fighting and platforming require attention to position, while puzzles ask him to understand how the space fits together. Returning to Inoa connects these excursions to people whose condition gives the next journey a reason beyond finding another treasure.

Jess shelters Alundra after the wreck, establishing a home from which the player repeatedly leaves and returns. As the nightmares continue, some villagers blame the newcomer for the tragedies around them. That changing reception makes a familiar place feel less secure. The story addresses death, faith and despair through its small community, with Kōhei Tanaka's music accompanying the contrast between refuge and danger. The North American release followed in 1997, with Europe receiving the game in 1998, and critics praised the characterisation and challenging puzzles. Alundra 2 appeared in 1999 as a separate adventure rather than a continuation of this village's story.
story_headings: Coming home to a darker story
